newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle near standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle near standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade remained near a standstill at midday Wednesday as bids at $63.00 per cwt continued to be passed by owners asking $65.00, feedlot sources said.
Several feedlot managers said they were confident that sales would be at least $64.00, unchanged from last week.
Fed cattle prices were seen bolstered by firm beef prices since July 10, with heavyweight choice climbing $4.05 per cwt as of Tuesday's close, market sources said.
Prices also were seen underpinned by a smaller number of cattle on showlists compared with last week, they said.
However, attempts to trade fed cattle above $64.00 were blunted by ideas beef prices were near a top, they said.
Beef prices reportedly have been supported by retail buying for advertising promotions at the end of the month, the market sources said.
Most retail buyers should be close to finished booking orders for the features, they said.
Packers also have been slow to buy cattle so far this week because they were said to have adequate supplies of live inventory following last week's fairly active trade, several cattle feeders said.
